steps.content: You are back in the dark alley where the attack took place. Dim light seeps through narrow gaps, barely illuminating your surroundings. This gloomy corner is worlds away from that bright town, yet it feels the closest to the somber truth right here.
You clutch the letter Dove gave you. Its edges are slightly worn, with Sheila's name printed on the envelope in an elegant script.
Dove said she found it the day after Sheila left. The connection between this lost family letter and that obsessive monster can't be mere coincidence.
Sheila's face and voice are still vivid in your memory, her tone almost echoing in your mind as you imagine her penning these words.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: Dear Mom and Dad, It's been so long since I last saw you. How's everything in Velvet Valley?
An innocuous greeting, followed by typical pleasantries and Sheila's hopeful musings about the future. However, the few last lines look increasingly crooked, scribbled in haste.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: I saw Antoine... and Sallie... No, I HEARD them... They're supposed to be in DisCity... Why are they back?

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: I followed their voices... and ended up here... There aren't any datura flowers here... And then I saw them, the monsters...
The once-elegant writing turns jagged, barely legible. Though it still looks like Sheila's handwriting, she must be scribbling these lines using some gravel soil she could grasp.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: The town is full of monsters... No one's ever left for DisCity...

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: She lied to us... No one's ever left...

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: The flowers... the datura flowers...
It looks like Sheila had been chased by monsters, and hastily jotted down what she knew upon finding a hiding spot.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: We can't see them with the flowers around... they can't hurt us! But I know, they're right next to me...!

Guided by Sheila's words, you walk into the alley. The once-withered vines now show fresh growth. The datura blossoms are blooming vibrantly, too perfect to be natural, as if someone has crafted them.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: The fragrance has numbed everyone... the monsters... even the Mania...
You continue your work, ripping off one datura stem after another. Each one crumbles into dry leaves before your eyes.
The handwriting in the letter becomes increasingly frenzied, the words barely discernible.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: I want to go home... but I can't... not anymore...

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: The flowers are wilting. They're coming...
As the floral scent fades, the growls of the monster grow clearer.
The monsters' been lurking all along, invisible to your eyes just as you are to its.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: My letter hasn't been sent yet. My parents still haven't heard from me...
Another patch of datura wilts. The dark alley is now devoid of white blossoms.
An agonized wail erupts as if from the depths of an abyss, threatening to drag everything into the underworldly void.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: I've promised Primrose... we'll go to DisCity together...

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: But I can't now... never...

The letter ends here. Only the taint of Mania lingers beyond those last words. It reminds you of what you sensed with your shackles on Sheila in her Corruptor form—the victim who tried to lead you to the truth, even risking being wiped out by Vautour Bleu.

You finally understand why back then Sheila lunged at you to cover your mouth and nose. You do so and try to block out the fragrance. As the scent fades, your vision clears. This town, once bathed in sunshine and brimming with hope, now reveals its true colors...

Oozing with Mania contamination, horrifying monsters roam aimlessly throughout Désir. They lurk by the flower beds, outside the bakery, down the local inn, haunting everywhere masked by the datura flowers' scent.
Beep. Belatedly, the Bureau's messages arrive:
█ The Outland Affairs Bureau has looked into it: No signs of activity within DisCity for any individuals on your list.
█ As for the other matter you said, we've got the results.

█ Datura flowers are native to the Outlands and have become extremely rare since the disasters began. They contain various toxic compounds that interfere with human neural function. Prolonged exposure can induce a sense of euphoria, even hallucinations.
█ Rumors run in WhiteSands; one says that those who encounter datura blossoms in an oasis will be forever bound to this desert.

While these Outland legends may not always be credible, one has been proven in Désir: No one ever makes it out of here. Their last hopes for DisCity have twisted into obsessive resentment and they are forever trapped in this purgatory as grotesque monsters that shun the light.
Gazing out from the alley, you see datura flowers planted everywhere in this quaint town. They adorn the diner, the post office, Vautour Bleu's balcony, even your own room.
So much effort has been poured into hiding the bitter truth—no one can ever reach DisCity.

You carefully tuck Sheila's letter into your coat and approach these specters laden with unresolved longing. They seem to sense something different in you, their mouths open as if to speak, but only silence follows, heavy with pain.
Their blood-red eyes are void of aggression, yet speak of their suffering; the residue of their resentment compels them to repeat a name over and over again: Vautour Bleu.

These were once residents of Désir, like everyone else you've seen, brimming with hope for the future and working tirelessly to save up for DisCity. Now, they're still the residents of this town, yet existing in a limbo beyond mortal sight.
You've suffered enough. Let me help you end this.
